evidence: frontend/apps/reality-web/src/lib/auth-context.tsx:78-106 — probeSsoSession() caches EVERY probe outcome for PROBE_CACHE_MS=2000ms, including the transient network-blip failure, directly contradicting that failure's own inline comment. The catch at :94-98 returns `{ ok: false }` and documents: 'Network blip — treat as transient, NOT as "logged out". Don\'t cache so the next mount can retry'. But the surrounding code ignores that intent: the IIFE's `.finally()` (:100-103) unconditionally sets `_cachedProbeAt = Date.now()`, and the outer body (:105) unconditionally runs `_cachedProbeResult = result;` for ALL results — the catch's transient `{ ok: false }` is cached identically to a legitimate unauthenticated `{ ok: false }` (the response-not-ok return at :92). The two failure modes are indistinguishable at the cache layer because they share the same `{ ok: false }` shape.

Consequence: for up to 2s after a single transient /api/v1/sso/session blip, every probeSsoSession() caller is served the stale cached failure from :80-82 (`if (_cachedProbeResult && now - _cachedProbeAt < PROBE_CACHE_MS) return _cachedProbeResult;`) and the documented 'next mount can retry' recovery never fires within that window, even if the network recovered immediately. For a cookie/SSO-only visitor (no stored bearer token) this is user-visible: checkSession() (:132-167) hits the bearer early-return only when getSession() is truthy, so a cookie user falls straight to `probeSsoSession()` at :155 and the else-branch at :163-164 calls `setUser(null)` on the cached `{ ok: false }` — the header renders the 'Sign in' control and will not self-correct until the 2s cache lapses AND something re-triggers a probe (remount / refreshSession), rather than on the very next check as the comment promises.

Note: the 2026-09-05 reality-web review explicitly cleared this helper ('probeSsoSession dedups + never clobbers state on a network blip') — that assessment covered the in-flight dedup and the return value but overlooked the result-cache write, so this caching defect is genuinely net-new (no probe-cache / PROBE_CACHE finding id exists in any prior signal file or in backlog.json). Fix (frontend-only, cloud-landable): only populate `_cachedProbeResult`/`_cachedProbeAt` for a definitive outcome — i.e. cache on `{ ok: true }` and on the response-not-ok `{ ok: false }` (unauthenticated) path, but skip the cache write for the catch (transient) path, e.g. by threading a `cacheable` flag out of the IIFE (true for both return statements, false in the catch) and guarding the `.finally` timestamp + the `_cachedProbeResult` assignment on it. Add a unit test: a first probe that rejects (fetch throws) must NOT be served from cache to a second probe fired <2s later — the second call must re-issue the fetch.
